reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:4558:docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:58:**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:6325:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-01/raw-output.txt:348:    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:6696:reviews/2026-07-12-gate-2-final/reviewer-a/iteration-05/raw-output.txt:182:58:**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:6838:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-03/raw-output.txt:9467:  1677	   556	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:7370:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:1146:    25	4. reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:7381:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:1469:   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:7504:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-04/raw-output.txt:1433:   556	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:7715:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-04/raw-output.txt:19077:   808	   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { join, dirname } from 'node:path';
import { bundlePaths, loadBundle, writeSnapshotIn, rotateJournalIn } from '../bundle/store.mjs';
import { withLock } from '../bundle/lock.mjs';
import { snapshot as gitSnapshot } from '../git/snapshot.mjs';
import { loadSignatures } from '../detect/signatures.mjs';
import { classify } from '../detect/classifier.mjs';
import { emitEnvelope, resolveRoot, usageError, parseFlagsStrict, platformError } from './shared.mjs';

const BUILTIN_SIGNATURES = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..', 'data', 'signatures.v1.json');

/**
 * Infer the reason class by running the reason text through the classifier
 * against the bundle's origin platform. No signature match reads as 'ok',
 * which is not a switch reason — degrade to null rather than mislabel.
 * @param {string} reason @param {string} platform @param {any} io
 * @returns {string | null}
 */
function inferReasonClass(reason, platform, io) {
  try {
    const table = loadSignatures({ builtinPath: BUILTIN_SIGNATURES }, io);
    const verdict = classify({ text: reason, exitCode: 0, platform, table, structured: null });
    return verdict.class === 'ok' ? null : verdict.class;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

/**
 * `baton finalize` — the narrative seal: records the switch reason, refreshes
 * git state, seals the bundle, and freezes this generation into history via a
 * 'finalize' journal rotation.
 * @param {string[]} args @param {any} io
 * @returns {Promise<number>}
 */
export async function cmdFinalize(args, io) {
  const parsed = parseFlagsStrict(args, { reason: 'string', 'reason-class': 'string', to: 'string' });
  if (parsed.error !== undefined) return usageError(io, parsed.flags, 'finalize', parsed.error);
  const flags = parsed.flags;
  const reason = typeof flags.reason === 'string' ? flags.reason : null;
  if (!reason) return usageError(io, flags, 'finalize', '--reason "<why you are switching>" is required');
  const toErr = platformError(flags.to);
  if (toErr) return usageError(io, flags, 'finalize', `--to: ${toErr}`);
  const REASON_CLASSES = ['usage-limit', 'auth', 'throttle', 'other-error'];
  if (flags['reason-class'] !== undefined && !REASON_CLASSES.includes(/** @type {string} */ (flags['reason-class']))) {
    return usageError(io, flags, 'finalize', `--reason-class must be one of ${REASON_CLASSES.join('|')}`);
  }

  const root = resolveRoot(io, flags);
  const paths = bundlePaths(root);
  const { bundle, warnings } = loadBundle(root, io);
  for (const w of warnings) io.stderr.write(`baton finalize: ${w}\n`);
  if (bundle === null) {
    const error = { code: 'no-bundle', msg: `no handoff bundle at ${paths.snapshot}; nothing to finalize` };
    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error });
    else io.stderr.write(`baton finalize: ${error.msg}\n`);
    return 1;
  }

  // Capture git BEFORE the lock — it is async and must not straddle the lock.
  const git = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
  if (git === null) io.stderr.write('baton finalize: git state unavailable — sealing with git marked unavailable (not the stale prior snapshot)\n');

  // ONE atomic locked span (iter-5 A2): the seal, snapshot write, and journal
  // rotation run under a SINGLE lock acquisition + fence, and the bundle is
  // RELOADED inside the lock. The old code loaded before the async git await
  // then sealed + wrote + rotated through separate locks, so a decision appended
  // during the await was sealed from a stale bundle and survived only in the
  // rotated journal. Reloading inside the lock includes it in the seal.
  const sealed = withLock(root, io, (token) => {
    const current = loadBundle(root, io).bundle;
    if (current === null) return null; // deleted concurrently between the checks
    const reasonClass =
      typeof flags['reason-class'] === 'string' ? flags['reason-class'] : inferReasonClass(reason, current.origin.platform, io);
    const s = {
      ...current,
      // NEVER seal the stale prior git snapshot (iter-4 I2 sibling): a receive
      // audits the seal's git against live state, so stale HEAD/dirty would emit
      // false "HEAD moved"/"dirty mismatch" warnings. On refresh failure seal an
      // explicit unavailable (null) git; receive re-derives it live regardless.
      git,
      updatedAt: io.now(),
      handoff: {
        ...current.handoff,
        status: 'sealed',
        reason,
        reasonClass,
        toPlatformHint: typeof flags.to === 'string' ? flags.to : null,
        finalizedAt: io.now(),
      },
    };
    writeSnapshotIn(root, s, io, token);
    rotateJournalIn(root, 'finalize', io, token);
    return s;
  });

  if (sealed === null) {
    const error = { code: 'no-bundle', msg: `handoff bundle vanished during finalize at ${paths.snapshot}` };
    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error });
    else io.stderr.write(`baton finalize: ${error.msg}\n`);
    return 1;
  }

  // Inference only matches verbatim harness banners; a natural paraphrase
  // seals reasonClass:null — and receive's role remap only auto-avoids the dead
  // platform on 'usage-limit'. Surface the gap instead of silently defeating
  // the failover heuristics (audit finding).
  if (sealed.handoff.reasonClass === null && flags['reason-class'] === undefined) {
    io.stderr.write(
      'baton finalize: no reason class inferred from the reason text — if this switch was forced, re-run with --reason-class <usage-limit|throttle|auth|other-error> so receive keeps roles off the exhausted platform\n',
    );
  }

  if (flags.json) {
    emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data: { bundlePath: paths.snapshot, handoffMdPath: paths.handoffMd } });
  } else {
    const rc = sealed.handoff.reasonClass;
    io.stdout.write(`sealed — reason: ${reason}${rc ? ` (${rc})` : ''}${sealed.handoff.toPlatformHint ? ` — next: ${sealed.handoff.toPlatformHint}` : ''}\n`);
  }
  return 0;
}

import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { join, dirname } from 'node:path';
import { loadBundle, writeSnapshotIn, rotateJournalIn } from '../bundle/store.mjs';
import { withLock } from '../bundle/lock.mjs';
import { loadConfig } from '../roles/matrix.mjs';
import { resolveRoles } from '../roles/resolve.mjs';
import { renderResumePrompt } from './prompt.mjs';
import { loadSignatures } from '../detect/signatures.mjs';
import { classify } from '../detect/classifier.mjs';
import { dedupeKey } from '../util/ids.mjs';

const BUILTIN_SIGNATURES = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..', 'data', 'signatures.v1.json');
const STALE_AFTER_MS = 12 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

/** @typedef {{platform: string, origin: string, reason: string, gitSnapshot: any, probes?: any, sessionHint: string, sessionUnstable?: boolean, reasonClass?: string}} ReceiveOpts */

/**
 * Classify the switch reason, KEEPING confidence (gate-2 iter-2 M4): a
 * low-confidence heuristic (e.g. Cursor's "quota exceeded") must not silently
 * drive an avoid[] decision — the caller warns and defers to explicit intake.
 * @param {string} reason @param {string} originPlatform @param {any} io
 * @returns {{class: string | null, confidence: string | null}}
 */
function classifyReason(reason, originPlatform, io) {
  try {
    const table = loadSignatures({ builtinPath: BUILTIN_SIGNATURES }, io);
    const verdict = classify({ text: reason, exitCode: 0, platform: originPlatform, table, structured: null });
    return verdict.class === 'ok' ? { class: null, confidence: null } : { class: verdict.class, confidence: verdict.confidence };
  } catch {
    return { class: null, confidence: null };
  }
}

/**
 * Effective intake: the sealed bundle already records who handed off and why,
 * so the 'unknown'/'unspecified' CLI sentinels default from it (audit finding:
 * the documented resume command rendered "Handed off from unknown" straight
 * after sealing a real origin/reason). Explicit intake always wins. Pure and
 * bundle-deterministic, so prepare and commit derive identical tokens.
 * @param {any} bundle @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @returns {ReceiveOpts}
 */
function effectiveIntake(bundle, opts) {
  const originSentinel = opts.origin === 'unknown' || opts.origin === undefined;
  const reasonSentinel = opts.reason === 'unspecified' || opts.reason === undefined;
  const sealedOrigin = typeof bundle?.origin?.platform === 'string' && bundle.origin.platform !== 'unknown' ? bundle.origin.platform : null;
  const sealedReason = typeof bundle?.handoff?.reason === 'string' && bundle.handoff.reason.length > 0 ? bundle.handoff.reason : null;
  return {
    ...opts,
    origin: originSentinel && sealedOrigin ? sealedOrigin : opts.origin,
    reason: reasonSentinel && sealedReason ? sealedReason : opts.reason,
  };
}

// The bound token inputs, in the fixed order the structured token serializes
// them. The human names power drift diagnosis: a stale-token rejection names
// exactly which input(s) moved instead of listing six guesses.
const TOKEN_FIELDS = /** @type {const} */ ([
  ['generation', 'bundle generation'],
  ['journalSeq', 'journal seq'],
  ['handoffStatus', 'handoff status'],
  ['receives', 'receive count'],
  ['origin', 'intake origin'],
  ['reason', 'intake reason'],
  ['reasonClass', 'intake reason-class'],
  ['configDigest', 'config'],
  ['gitDigest', 'git state'],
  ['probesDigest', 'probe cache'],
  ['platform', 'target platform'],
  ['sessionHint', 'target session'],
]);
const TOKEN_PREFIX = 'rcpt1';

/**
 * The revision fingerprint the receipt token derives from. Every field is a
 * bound input: any drift between prepare and commit re-derives a different
 * token, so a stale receipt can never commit (plan §Concurrency).
 * @param {string} root @param {any} bundle @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
 * @returns {Record<string, any>}
 */
function tokenInputs(root, bundle, opts, io) {
  let configDigest = 'absent';
  try {
    configDigest = dedupeKey(io.fs.readFileSync(`${root}/baton.config.json`, 'utf8'));
  } catch {
    // no config — 'absent' is itself a bound value
  }
  return {
    generation: bundle.generation,
    journalSeq: bundle.journalSeq,
    // The seal state is a bound input too (gate-2 fix): a competing receiver
    // that lands between this token's derivation and its commit changes
    // status/receive_log, so the loser's token cannot re-derive.
    handoffStatus: bundle.handoff?.status ?? null,
    receives: Array.isArray(bundle.handoff?.receive_log) ? bundle.handoff.receive_log.length : 0,
    origin: opts.origin,
    reason: opts.reason,
    // Explicit --reason-class is a bound intake input (gate-2 iter-2 M4): it
    // changes the avoid[] decision, so a change between prepare and commit is
    // drift that must re-prepare.
    reasonClass: opts.reasonClass ?? null,
    configDigest,
    gitDigest: dedupeKey(opts.gitSnapshot ?? null),
    probesDigest: dedupeKey(opts.probes ?? null),
    platform: opts.platform,
    sessionHint: opts.sessionHint,
  };
}

/**
 * Structured receipt token: a fixed-order join of per-input digests. Equality
 * still gates commit exactly as the old opaque hash did; the structure only
 * buys DIAGNOSIS — a mismatch can name the drifted input(s).
 * @param {string} root @param {any} bundle @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
 */
function deriveToken(root, bundle, opts, io) {
  const inputs = tokenInputs(root, bundle, opts, io);
  return `${TOKEN_PREFIX}.` + TOKEN_FIELDS.map(([key]) => dedupeKey(inputs[key] ?? null).slice(0, 10)).join('.');
}

/**
 * Name the inputs whose digests differ between two structured tokens.
 * @param {string} presented @param {string} expected @returns {string[]}
 */
function driftedInputs(presented, expected) {
  const a = presented.split('.');
  const b = expected.split('.');
  if (a[0] !== TOKEN_PREFIX || b[0] !== TOKEN_PREFIX || a.length !== b.length) return [];
  return TOKEN_FIELDS.filter((_, i) => a[i + 1] !== b[i + 1]).map(([, name]) => name);
}

/**
 * @param {any} bundle @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
 * @returns {string[]} staleness/degradation warnings
 */
function stalenessWarnings(bundle, opts, io) {
  /** @type {string[]} */
  const warnings = [];
  if (bundle.handoff.status === 'open') {
    warnings.push('source bundle is unsealed (open) — the handoff was never finalized; treating this as a degraded (limit-death) receive');
  }
  const ref = bundle.handoff.finalizedAt ?? bundle.updatedAt;
  const ageMs = Date.parse(io.now()) - Date.parse(ref);
  if (Number.isFinite(ageMs) && ageMs > STALE_AFTER_MS) {
    warnings.push(`bundle finalized ${Math.round(ageMs / 3_600_000)}h ago (staleness threshold 12h) — re-verify before continuing`);
  }
  const g = opts.gitSnapshot;
  if (g && bundle.git) {
    if (bundle.git.headSha !== g.headSha) {
      warnings.push(`HEAD moved since capture: bundle recorded ${bundle.git.headSha}, working tree now ${g.headSha}`);
    }
    if (bundle.git.dirty !== g.dirty) {
      warnings.push(`dirty-state mismatch: bundle captured dirty=${bundle.git.dirty}, working tree now dirty=${g.dirty}`);
    }
  }
  return warnings;
}

/**
 * Phase 1 of the receive transaction: validate, resolve roles, render the
 * resume prompt, and return a one-time receipt token. Mutates NOTHING — the
 * token is self-contained (a fingerprint hash), never a persisted record.
 * @param {string} root @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
 * @returns {{token: string, prompt: string, assignments: Record<string, any>, warnings: string[]}}
 */
export function prepare(root, opts, io) {
  const { bundle, warnings: loadWarnings } = loadBundle(root, io);
  if (bundle === null) throw new Error(`no handoff bundle under ${root}/.handoff — nothing to receive`);
  opts = effectiveIntake(bundle, opts);

  const warnings = [...loadWarnings, ...stalenessWarnings(bundle, opts, io)];

  const { config, errors } = loadConfig(root, io);
  /** @type {Record<string, any>} */
  let assignments = {};
  if (config) {
    // The dead origin comes from the BUNDLE first (its sealed reasonClass and
    // recorded origin platform); typed intake only fills the gaps — a user
    // should not need to retype the verbatim limit string to keep roles off
    // the platform that died (gate-2 reviewer-b finding 4). Confidence gates
    // auto-avoidance (gate-2 iter-2 M4): an explicit --reason-class or a sealed
    // reasonClass is trusted; a live text classification only auto-avoids at
    // medium+ confidence, else it warns and defers to explicit intake.
    let reasonClass;
    let confidence;
    if (typeof opts.reasonClass === 'string') {
      reasonClass = opts.reasonClass;
      confidence = 'high'; // explicit user intake
    } else if (typeof bundle.handoff?.reasonClass === 'string') {
      reasonClass = bundle.handoff.reasonClass;
      confidence = 'high'; // trusted seal
    } else {
      const v = classifyReason(opts.reason, opts.origin, io);
      reasonClass = v.class;
      confidence = v.confidence;
    }
    const deadOrigin =
      typeof bundle.origin?.platform === 'string' && bundle.origin.platform !== 'unknown' ? bundle.origin.platform : opts.origin;
    /** @type {string[]} */
    let avoid = [];
    if (reasonClass === 'usage-limit') {
      if (confidence === 'low') {
        warnings.push(
          `the switch reason matched a usage-limit heuristic only at LOW confidence — not auto-avoiding ${deadOrigin}; pass --reason-class usage-limit to confirm the failover away from it`,
        );
      } else {
        avoid = [deadOrigin];
      }
    }
    assignments = resolveRoles({ config, to: opts.platform, avoid, nativeOnly: false, probes: opts.probes ?? null }).assignments;
  } else {
    warnings.push(`role matrix unavailable (${errors.map((e) => e.msg).join('; ')}) — no role table in this prompt`);
  }

  const prompt = renderResumePrompt({ bundle, assignments, warnings, origin: opts.origin, reason: opts.reason });
  return { token: deriveToken(root, bundle, opts, io), prompt, assignments, warnings };
}

/**
 * Phase 2: one atomic transition. Re-derives every bound input from current
 * disk state + opts and rejects ANY drift (throws, zero mutation). On match:
 * writes the received seal, archives it via a 'receive' rotation, then opens a
 * fresh writable generation owned by the receiving platform/session.
 * @param {string} root @param {string} token @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
 * @returns {{adopted: boolean, generation: number, archivedTo: string | null, alreadyCommitted?: boolean}}
 */
export function commit(root, token, opts, io) {
  // ONE operation-scoped lock across revalidation and every mutation (gate-2
  // fix: reviewers a#1/b#11): two competing receivers serialize here, and the
  // loser's re-derivation sees the winner's generation/status/receive_log.
  return withLock(root, io, (fence) => commitLocked(root, token, opts, io, fence));
}

/**
 * @param {string} root @param {string} token @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io @param {string} fence
 * @returns {{adopted: boolean, generation: number, archivedTo: string | null, alreadyCommitted?: boolean}}
 */
function commitLocked(root, token, opts, io, fence) {
  const { bundle } = loadBundle(root, io);
  if (bundle === null) throw new Error(`no handoff bundle under ${root}/.handoff — nothing to receive; run receive --prepare first`);
  opts = effectiveIntake(bundle, opts);

  const expected = deriveToken(root, bundle, opts, io);
  if (expected !== token) {
    // Idempotency first (audit finding: duplicate-receive corruption): if THIS
    // exact receipt already landed — its digest is recorded on a receive_log
    // entry — the retry is a lost-output re-send, not drift. Report success
    // with zero mutation instead of sending the model into a re-prepare +
    // re-commit loop that executes a second full receive.
    const receipt = dedupeKey(token).slice(0, 16);
    const landed = Array.isArray(bundle.handoff?.receive_log) && bundle.handoff.receive_log.some((/** @type {any} */ e) => e?.receipt === receipt);
    if (landed) {
      return { adopted: false, alreadyCommitted: true, generation: bundle.generation, archivedTo: null };
    }
    const drifted = driftedInputs(token, expected);
    const detail = drifted.length > 0 ? `drifted input(s): ${drifted.join(', ')}` : 'a bound input drifted since prepare';
    throw new Error(
      `receipt token is stale — ${detail}. Re-prepare and retry, passing the SAME intake flags (--origin/--reason/--reason-class) to both prepare and --commit`,
    );
  }

  const degraded = bundle.handoff.status !== 'sealed';
  const receiveEntry = {
    origin: opts.origin,
    reason: opts.reason,
    at: io.now(),
    // The receipt digest keys the idempotent-retry detection above.
    receipt: dedupeKey(token).slice(0, 16),
    ...(degraded ? { degradedSeal: true } : {}),
  };

  // The degraded seal must NOT persist a LOW-confidence classification (iter-3
  // F10): a sealed reasonClass is trusted as high-confidence by the next
  // prepare, so laundering a low-confidence heuristic here would silently
  // auto-avoid the origin one hop later. Explicit intake is high-confidence and
  // seals; a live classification seals ONLY at medium+ confidence, else null
  // (the next receive re-classifies the reason text at its true confidence).
  let sealedReasonClass = null;
  if (degraded) {
    if (typeof opts.reasonClass === 'string') {
      sealedReasonClass = opts.reasonClass;

    ...overrides,
  };
}

function makeRepoIo({ status = 'open', originPlatform = 'codex', overrides = {}, execFile, extraSignatures = [] } = {}) {
  const io = makeIo({
    now: T0,
    host: 'loop-host',
    pid: 4242,
    startTime: 111000,
    fencingSeed: 1,
    files: {
      [SIG_ABS]: sigContentWith(extraSignatures),
      '/repo/baton.config.json': JSON.stringify(CONFIG, null, 2),
      '/repo/.handoff/bundle.json': JSON.stringify(bundleFixture({ status, originPlatform, overrides }), null, 2) + '\n',
    },
  });
  if (execFile) io.execFile = execFile;
  return io;
}

const parsedConfig = (io) => loadConfig('/repo', io).config;
const asg = (platform, role, model, effort = null) => ({ platform, role, model, effort, mode: platform === 'codex' ? 'native' : 'delegated' });

// A git execFile whose HEAD is chosen per rev-parse-HEAD call (the drift seam),
// and which counts those calls so a test can pin the exact number of
// prepare->commit windows. gitSnapshot reads clean status/diffs.
function gitExec(headForCall) {
  let headCalls = 0;
  const fn = (/** @type {string} */ cmd, /** @type {string[]} */ args = []) => {
    if (cmd !== 'git') return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error('spawn ENOENT'), { code: 'ENOENT' }));
    const key = args.join(' ');
    if (key === 'rev-parse HEAD') {
      headCalls += 1;
      return Promise.resolve({ stdout: headForCall(headCalls) + '\n', stderr: '' });
    }
    const out = key === 'rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD' ? 'main' : '';
    return Promise.resolve({ stdout: out + '\n', stderr: '' });
  };
  fn.headCalls = () => headCalls;
  return fn;
}

// Spy every write touching .handoff/loop.
function spyLoopWrites(io) {
  const writes = /** @type {string[]} */ ([]);
  const note = (/** @type {any} */ p) => { if (typeof p === 'string' && p.startsWith('/repo/.handoff/loop')) writes.push(p); };
  for (const m of ['writeFileSync', 'appendFileSync', 'mkdirSync', 'unlinkSync', 'rmSync']) {
    const real = io.fs[m].bind(io.fs);
    io.fs[m] = (/** @type {any} */ p, /** @type {any} */ a) => { note(p); return real(p, a); };
  }
  for (const m of ['renameSync', 'copyFileSync']) {
    const real = io.fs[m].bind(io.fs);
    io.fs[m] = (/** @type {any} */ from, /** @type {any} */ to) => { note(from); note(to); return real(from, to); };
  }
  return writes;
}

const historyFreezes = (io) => {
  const dir = bundlePaths('/repo').historyDir;
  if (!io.fs.existsSync(dir)) return [];
  return io.fs.readdirSync(dir).map((/** @type {string} */ n) => ({ name: n, data: JSON.parse(io.fs.readFileSync(`${dir}/${n}`, 'utf8')) }));
};

// A base input for a usage-limit failover of the `implementer` role on codex.
function usageLimitInput(io, over = {}) {
  return {
    root: '/repo',
    io,
    config: parsedConfig(io),
    role: 'implementer',
    assignment: asg('codex', 'implementer', 'gpt-5.6-sol', 'xhigh'),
    transcript: CODEX_LIMIT,
    exitCode: 1,
    sessionHint: 'loop-run1',
    probes: null,
    avoid: [],
    avoidEntries: [],
    attempt: 1,
    loopState: { runId: 'run1', phaseIndex: 7, gate: 'subtask-review', note: POSITION_SENTINEL },
    ...over,
  };
}

describe('runFailover — non-limit exits: retry once, then park', () => {
  it('other-error on the FIRST attempt -> {action:retry}', async () => {
    const { runFailover } = M();
    const io = makeRepoIo();
    const d = await runFailover(usageLimitInput(io, { transcript: 'Error: build failed with 3 errors', exitCode: 1, attempt: 1 }));
    assert.equal(d.class, 'other-error');
    assert.equal(d.action, 'retry', 'a generic failure retries once');
  });

  it('other-error on the SECOND attempt -> {action:park} (retry-once-then-park)', async () => {
    const { runFailover } = M();
    const io = makeRepoIo();
    const d = await runFailover(usageLimitInput(io, { transcript: 'Error: build failed', exitCode: 1, attempt: 2 }));
    assert.equal(d.class, 'other-error');
    assert.equal(d.action, 'park', 'a second consecutive generic failure parks');
    assert.ok(typeof d.reason === 'string' && d.reason.length > 0, 'the park records a reason');
  });

  it('a non-limit failure NEVER seals or receives (no bundle transition)', async () => {
    const { runFailover } = M();
    const io = makeRepoIo();
    await runFailover(usageLimitInput(io, { transcript: 'Error: build failed', exitCode: 1, attempt: 1 }));
    const live = loadBundle('/repo', io).bundle;
    assert.equal(live.generation, 1, 'no generation opened for a non-limit failure');
    assert.equal(historyFreezes(io).length, 0, 'no seal/receive freeze for a non-limit failure');
  });
});

    61	  const git = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
    62	  if (git === null) io.stderr.write('baton finalize: git state unavailable — sealing with git marked unavailable (not the stale prior snapshot)\n');
    63	
    64	  // ONE atomic locked span (iter-5 A2): the seal, snapshot write, and journal
    65	  // rotation run under a SINGLE lock acquisition + fence, and the bundle is
    66	  // RELOADED inside the lock. The old code loaded before the async git await

   132	 * @param {any} bundle @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
   133	 * @returns {string[]} staleness/degradation warnings
   134	 */
   135	function stalenessWarnings(bundle, opts, io) {
   136	  /** @type {string[]} */
   137	  const warnings = [];
   138	  if (bundle.handoff.status === 'open') {
   139	    warnings.push('source bundle is unsealed (open) — the handoff was never finalized; treating this as a degraded (limit-death) receive');
   140	  }
   141	  const ref = bundle.handoff.finalizedAt ?? bundle.updatedAt;
   142	  const ageMs = Date.parse(io.now()) - Date.parse(ref);
   143	  if (Number.isFinite(ageMs) && ageMs > STALE_AFTER_MS) {
   144	    warnings.push(`bundle finalized ${Math.round(ageMs / 3_600_000)}h ago (staleness threshold 12h) — re-verify before continuing`);
   145	  }
   146	  const g = opts.gitSnapshot;
   147	  if (g && bundle.git) {
   148	    if (bundle.git.headSha !== g.headSha) {
   149	      warnings.push(`HEAD moved since capture: bundle recorded ${bundle.git.headSha}, working tree now ${g.headSha}`);
   150	    }
   151	    if (bundle.git.dirty !== g.dirty) {
   152	      warnings.push(`dirty-state mismatch: bundle captured dirty=${bundle.git.dirty}, working tree now dirty=${g.dirty}`);
   153	    }
   154	  }
   155	  return warnings;
   156	}

   158	/**
   159	 * Phase 1 of the receive transaction: validate, resolve roles, render the
   160	 * resume prompt, and return a one-time receipt token. Mutates NOTHING — the
   161	 * token is self-contained (a fingerprint hash), never a persisted record.
   162	 * @param {string} root @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
   163	 * @returns {{token: string, prompt: string, assignments: Record<string, any>, warnings: string[]}}
   164	 */
   165	export function prepare(root, opts, io) {
   166	  const { bundle, warnings: loadWarnings } = loadBundle(root, io);
   167	  if (bundle === null) throw new Error(`no handoff bundle under ${root}/.handoff — nothing to receive`);
   168	  opts = effectiveIntake(bundle, opts);
   169	
   170	  const warnings = [...loadWarnings, ...stalenessWarnings(bundle, opts, io)];
   171	
   172	  const { config, errors } = loadConfig(root, io);
   173	  /** @type {Record<string, any>} */
   174	  let assignments = {};
   175	  if (config) {
   176	    // The dead origin comes from the BUNDLE first (its sealed reasonClass and
   177	    // recorded origin platform); typed intake only fills the gaps — a user
   178	    // should not need to retype the verbatim limit string to keep roles off
   179	    // the platform that died (gate-2 reviewer-b finding 4). Confidence gates
   180	    // auto-avoidance (gate-2 iter-2 M4): an explicit --reason-class or a sealed
   181	    // reasonClass is trusted; a live text classification only auto-avoids at
   182	    // medium+ confidence, else it warns and defers to explicit intake.
   183	    let reasonClass;
   184	    let confidence;
   185	    if (typeof opts.reasonClass === 'string') {
   186	      reasonClass = opts.reasonClass;
   187	      confidence = 'high'; // explicit user intake
   188	    } else if (typeof bundle.handoff?.reasonClass === 'string') {
   189	      reasonClass = bundle.handoff.reasonClass;
   190	      confidence = 'high'; // trusted seal
   191	    } else {
   192	      const v = classifyReason(opts.reason, opts.origin, io);
   193	      reasonClass = v.class;
   194	      confidence = v.confidence;
   195	    }
   196	    const deadOrigin =
   197	      typeof bundle.origin?.platform === 'string' && bundle.origin.platform !== 'unknown' ? bundle.origin.platform : opts.origin;
   198	    /** @type {string[]} */
   199	    let avoid = [];
   200	    if (reasonClass === 'usage-limit') {
   201	      if (confidence === 'low') {
   202	        warnings.push(
   203	          `the switch reason matched a usage-limit heuristic only at LOW confidence — not auto-avoiding ${deadOrigin}; pass --reason-class usage-limit to confirm the failover away from it`,
   204	        );
   205	      } else {
   206	        avoid = [deadOrigin];
   207	      }
   208	    }
   209	    assignments = resolveRoles({ config, to: opts.platform, avoid, nativeOnly: false, probes: opts.probes ?? null }).assignments;
   210	  } else {
   211	    warnings.push(`role matrix unavailable (${errors.map((e) => e.msg).join('; ')}) — no role table in this prompt`);
   212	  }
   213	
   214	  const prompt = renderResumePrompt({ bundle, assignments, warnings, origin: opts.origin, reason: opts.reason });
   215	  return { token: deriveToken(root, bundle, opts, io), prompt, assignments, warnings };
   216	}
   217	
   218	/**
   219	 * Phase 2: one atomic transition. Re-derives every bound input from current
   220	 * disk state + opts and rejects ANY drift (throws, zero mutation). On match:
   221	 * writes the received seal, archives it via a 'receive' rotation, then opens a
   222	 * fresh writable generation owned by the receiving platform/session.
   223	 * @param {string} root @param {string} token @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
   224	 * @returns {{adopted: boolean, generation: number, archivedTo: string | null, alreadyCommitted?: boolean}}
   225	 */
   226	export function commit(root, token, opts, io) {
   227	  // ONE operation-scoped lock across revalidation and every mutation (gate-2
   228	  // fix: reviewers a#1/b#11): two competing receivers serialize here, and the
   229	  // loser's re-derivation sees the winner's generation/status/receive_log.
   230	  return withLock(root, io, (fence) => commitLocked(root, token, opts, io, fence));
   231	}
   232	
   233	/**
   234	 * @param {string} root @param {string} token @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io @param {string} fence
   235	 * @returns {{adopted: boolean, generation: number, archivedTo: string | null, alreadyCommitted?: boolean}}
   236	 */
   237	function commitLocked(root, token, opts, io, fence) {
   238	  const { bundle } = loadBundle(root, io);
   239	  if (bundle === null) throw new Error(`no handoff bundle under ${root}/.handoff — nothing to receive; run receive --prepare first`);
   240	  opts = effectiveIntake(bundle, opts);
   241	
   242	  const expected = deriveToken(root, bundle, opts, io);
   243	  if (expected !== token) {
   244	    // Idempotency first (audit finding: duplicate-receive corruption): if THIS
   245	    // exact receipt already landed — its digest is recorded on a receive_log
   246	    // entry — the retry is a lost-output re-send, not drift. Report success
   247	    // with zero mutation instead of sending the model into a re-prepare +
   248	    // re-commit loop that executes a second full receive.
   249	    const receipt = dedupeKey(token).slice(0, 16);
   250	    const landed = Array.isArray(bundle.handoff?.receive_log) && bundle.handoff.receive_log.some((/** @type {any} */ e) => e?.receipt === receipt);
   251	    if (landed) {
   252	      return { adopted: false, alreadyCommitted: true, generation: bundle.generation, archivedTo: null };
   253	    }
   254	    const drifted = driftedInputs(token, expected);
   255	    const detail = drifted.length > 0 ? `drifted input(s): ${drifted.join(', ')}` : 'a bound input drifted since prepare';
   256	    throw new Error(
   257	      `receipt token is stale — ${detail}. Re-prepare and retry, passing the SAME intake flags (--origin/--reason/--reason-class) to both prepare and --commit`,
   258	    );
   259	  }
   260	
   261	  const degraded = bundle.handoff.status !== 'sealed';
   262	  const receiveEntry = {
   263	    origin: opts.origin,
   264	    reason: opts.reason,
   265	    at: io.now(),
   266	    // The receipt digest keys the idempotent-retry detection above.
   267	    receipt: dedupeKey(token).slice(0, 16),
   268	    ...(degraded ? { degradedSeal: true } : {}),
   269	  };
   270	
   271	  // The degraded seal must NOT persist a LOW-confidence classification (iter-3
   272	  // F10): a sealed reasonClass is trusted as high-confidence by the next
   273	  // prepare, so laundering a low-confidence heuristic here would silently
   274	  // auto-avoid the origin one hop later. Explicit intake is high-confidence and
   275	  // seals; a live classification seals ONLY at medium+ confidence, else null
   276	  // (the next receive re-classifies the reason text at its true confidence).
   277	  let sealedReasonClass = null;
   278	  if (degraded) {
   279	    if (typeof opts.reasonClass === 'string') {
   280	      sealedReasonClass = opts.reasonClass;
   281	    } else {
   282	      const v = classifyReason(opts.reason, opts.origin, io);
   283	      sealedReasonClass = v.confidence === 'low' ? null : v.class;
   284	    }
   285	  }
   286	
   287	  const receivedSeal = {
   288	    ...bundle,
   289	    updatedAt: io.now(),
   290	    handoff: {
   291	      ...bundle.handoff,
   292	      status: 'received',
   293	      ...(degraded
   294	        ? {
   295	            reason: opts.reason,
   296	            reasonClass: sealedReasonClass,
   297	            finalizedAt: io.now(),
   298	          }
   299	        : {}),
   300	      receive_log: [...bundle.handoff.receive_log, receiveEntry],
   301	    },
   302	  };
   303	
   304	  // Freeze order: the received seal is written first so the 'receive' rotation
   305	  // archives exactly that state (never the pre-commit bundle). All three
   306	  // mutations run under the SAME lock acquisition, fence-checked per write.
   307	  writeSnapshotIn(root, receivedSeal, io, fence);
   308	  const archivedTo = rotateJournalIn(root, 'receive', io, fence);
   309	
   310	  const { config } = loadConfig(root, io);
   311	  const next = {
   312	    ...receivedSeal,
   313	    generation: bundle.generation + 1,
   314	    origin: {
   315	      platform: opts.platform,
   316	      model: config?.defaults?.[opts.platform] ?? 'unknown',
   317	      sessionHint: opts.sessionHint,
   318	      unstable: opts.sessionUnstable === true,
   319	    },
   320	    // The fresh writable generation has NO switch reason yet (iter-4 I3): the
   321	    // sealed reason/reasonClass/finalizedAt/toPlatformHint describe the PRIOR
   322	    // handoff, not this one. Carrying them forward made the next prepare trust a
   323	    // stale class as a high-confidence seal (silently auto-avoiding the healthy
   324	    // adopted origin) and poisoned both the 12 h staleness reference and the
   325	    // sessionStart limit-hit signal. Keep only receive_log (the audit chain).
   326	    handoff: { ...receivedSeal.handoff, status: 'open', reason: null, reasonClass: null, finalizedAt: null, toPlatformHint: null },
   327	  };
   328	  writeSnapshotIn(root, next, io, fence);
   329	
   330	  return { adopted: true, generation: next.generation, archivedTo };
   331	}

     1	/**
     2	 * Pure, explainable role resolution over the committed matrix. Every decision
     3	 * is auditable: chosen entries carry their chainIndex; passed-over entries land
     4	 * in skipped[] with a why. avoid[] population is the caller's job.
     5	 * @param {{config: any, to: string, avoid?: string[], avoidEntries?: Array<{platform: string, model: string}>, nativeOnly?: boolean, probes?: Record<string, {capability: string, outcome: string}> | null}} input
     6	 * @returns {{assignments: Record<string, any>, notes: string[]}}
     7	 */
     8	export function resolveRoles({ config, to, avoid = [], avoidEntries = [], nativeOnly = false, probes = null }) {
     9	  /** @type {string[]} */
    10	  const notes = [];
    11	
    12	  /**
    13	   * The eligibility verdict for a platform, or null when eligible.
    14	   * @param {string} platform @returns {string | null}
    15	   */
    16	  function skipReason(platform) {
    17	    if (avoid.includes(platform)) return 'avoided';
    18	    if (!(platform in (config.platforms ?? {}))) return 'unknown-platform';
    19	    if (config.platforms[platform]?.enabled === false) return 'disabled';
    20	    if (probes && probes[platform]) {
    21	      const { capability, outcome } = probes[platform];
    22	      if (outcome === 'rate-limited') return 'rate-limited';
    23	      if (capability === 'not-installed') return 'not-installed';
    24	      // 'installed' means installation was PROVEN but the probe was capped there
    25	      // (capOnSuccess) — authentication is UNVERIFIED, not verified-failed. Only
    26	      // a probe that ran and did NOT succeed (outcome !== 'ok') is a verified
    27	      // auth/reachability failure worth skipping; a capped success stays
    28	      // selectable and is flagged degraded below (iter-3 F1, plan §Role matrix).
    29	      if (capability === 'installed' && outcome !== 'ok') return 'unauthenticated';
    30	    }
    31	    return null;
    32	  }
    33	
    34	  // A selection is degraded when its availability is UNVERIFIED (gate-2 iter-2
    35	  // M3, iter-3 F1): with no probe cache at all, resolution is offline and EVERY
    36	  // selection is degraded (plan: "Offline resolution always succeeds, flagged
    37	  // degraded"); with a partial cache, platforms the cache is missing are; and a
    38	  // platform probed only to 'installed' (auth unverified, e.g. a --version
    39	  // success) is degraded even though it stays selectable.
    40	  /** @param {string} platform */
    41	  const probeUnverified = (platform) => {
    42	    if (probes == null || !probes[platform]) return true;
    43	    const { capability, outcome } = probes[platform];
    44	    // Degraded when ANY required dimension is unverified: a capped 'installed'
    45	    // (auth never confirmed) OR a non-ok outcome (iter-4 I6) — a selectable
    46	    // platform whose last probe ERRORED or TIMED OUT is presented as
    47	    // reachability-verified otherwise, which is exactly the silent-degradation
    48	    // the plan's degraded flag exists to surface. (rate-limited is skipped, not
    49	    // selected, so it never reaches here.)
    50	    return capability === 'installed' || outcome !== 'ok';
    51	  };
    52	
    53	  // Entry-level avoidance (plan §Model-level failover): a specific
    54	  // {platform, model} tuple is dead (e.g. account-tier rejected) while its
    55	  // platform stays usable. Matching is on model IDENTITY — an @effort suffix
    56	  // on either side is ignored — and requires BOTH dimensions, so the same
    57	  // model name on another platform is never caught.
    58	  /** @param {any} m */
    59	  const baseModel = (m) => (typeof m === 'string' ? m.split('@')[0] : m);
    60	  /** @param {string} platform @param {string} model */
    61	  const entryAvoided = (platform, model) =>
    62	    avoidEntries.some((a) => a?.platform === platform && baseModel(a?.model) === baseModel(model));
    63	
    64	  /** @type {Record<string, any>} */
    65	  const assignments = {};
    66	  for (const [role, chain] of Object.entries(config.roles)) {
    67	    /** @type {any[]} */
    68	    const skipped = [];
    69	    /** @type {any} */
    70	    let assignment = null;
    71	
    72	    for (let i = 0; i < chain.length; i += 1) {
    73	      const entry = chain[i];
    74	      if (nativeOnly && entry.platform !== to) {
    75	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why: 'non-native' });
    76	        continue;
    77	      }
    78	      const why = skipReason(entry.platform);
    79	      if (why) {
    80	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why });
    81	        continue;
    82	      }
    83	      // After skipReason so a dual match keeps the platform-level label.
    84	      if (entryAvoided(entry.platform, entry.model)) {
    85	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why: 'avoided-entry' });
    86	        continue;
    87	      }
    88	      assignment = {
    89	        platform: entry.platform,
    90	        model: entry.model,
    91	        effort: entry.effort ?? null,
    92	        mode: entry.platform === to ? 'native' : 'delegated',
    93	        chainIndex: i,
    94	        skipped,
    95	      };
    96	      if (probeUnverified(entry.platform)) assignment.degraded = true;
    97	      break;
    98	    }
    99	
   100	    if (!assignment && nativeOnly) {
   101	      // Forced-default is only valid when the destination itself is eligible.
   102	      const whyTo = skipReason(to);
   103	      const model = config.defaults?.[to];
   104	      if (!whyTo && typeof model === 'string') {
   105	        assignment = { platform: to, model, effort: null, mode: 'forced-default', chainIndex: null, skipped };
   106	        if (probeUnverified(to)) assignment.degraded = true;
   107	      }
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    if (!assignment) {
   111	      assignment = { platform: null, model: null, effort: null, mode: 'unavailable', chainIndex: null, skipped };
   112	    }
   113	    assignments[role] = assignment;
   114	  }
   115	
   116	  return { assignments, notes };
   117	}

    49	    // unstable so the receiving session's first real hook checkpoint adopts
    50	    // ownership instead of being rejected as foreign (gate-2 fix 2).
    51	    sessionUnstable: !hasSession,
    52	  };
    53	
    54	  // A lost commit token (empty shell var, --commit followed by another flag)
    55	  // must be a loud usage error — falling through to the read-only prepare path
    56	  // with exit 0 convinced models a commit landed when nothing mutated.
    57	  if (flags.commit !== undefined && typeof flags.commit !== 'string') {
    58	    return usageError(io, flags, 'receive', '--commit requires the receipt token printed by prepare (the token argument is missing)');
    59	  }
    60	  if (flags.commit !== undefined && flags.prepare !== undefined) {
    61	    return usageError(io, flags, 'receive', '--prepare and --commit are mutually exclusive phases');
    62	  }
    63	
    64	  if (typeof flags.commit === 'string') {
    65	    try {
    66	      const res = commit(root, flags.commit, opts, io);
    67	      if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data: res });
    68	      else if (res.alreadyCommitted === true) io.stdout.write(`already committed — generation ${res.generation} is open on ${platform}; nothing to redo\n`);
    69	      else io.stdout.write(`received — generation ${res.generation} open on ${platform}; archived ${res.archivedTo}\n`);
    70	      return 0;
    71	    } catch (err) {
    72	      const msg = /** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? String(err);
    73	      if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error: { code: 'commit-rejected', msg } });
    74	      else io.stderr.write(`baton receive: ${msg}\n`);
    75	      return 1;
    76	    }
    77	  }
    78	
    79	  /** @type {ReturnType<typeof prepare>} */
    80	  let prepared;
    81	  try {
    82	    prepared = prepare(root, opts, io);
    83	  } catch (err) {
    84	    const msg = /** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? String(err);
    85	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error: { code: 'prepare-failed', msg } });
    86	    else io.stderr.write(`baton receive: ${msg}\n`);
    87	    return 1;
    88	  }
    89	
    90	  if (flags['print-prompt'] === true) {
    91	    // --json wraps the prompt in the envelope (gate-2 iter-2 M6); the bare
    92	    // form stays raw markdown — the adapter hook fallback path is unchanged.
    93	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data: { prompt: prepared.prompt, warnings: prepared.warnings } });
    94	    else io.stdout.write(prepared.prompt);
    95	    return 0;
    96	  }
    97	
    98	  if (flags.json) {
    99	    emitEnvelope(io, {
   100	      ok: true,
   101	      data: { token: prepared.token, prompt: prepared.prompt, assignments: prepared.assignments, warnings: prepared.warnings },
   102	    });
   103	  } else {
   104	    for (const w of prepared.warnings) io.stderr.write(`baton receive: ${w}\n`);
   105	    io.stderr.write(`baton receive: token ${prepared.token}\n`);
   106	    io.stdout.write(prepared.prompt);
   107	  }
   108	  return 0;
   109	}
